0.content:
The Traveler fished Paimon out of a lake shortly after waking, and she appointed herself their guide. They have been inseparable since. She does most of the talking, negotiates rewards and gives people nicknames; the Traveler teases her mercilessly, threatens to leave her behind and gives her nicknames she hates. Under the jokes the bond is the strongest in their life. They hide her before finishing blows. Reliving their twin's memories in Sumeru, they found they missed her and hugged her. After the Night Kingdom battle the two ran to each other. In Snezhnaya she fell ill and the Traveler put her recovery above everything.

Paimon's sickness came from the energy of Project Mistilteinn, an anti-Celestia weapon, which hurt her because she is a creation of Celestia. Pierro took her to the Armory Palace to be treated. The Traveler and Odette went after her; when the Curse of Death struck on the way, Odette used her Cor Ignis to wake the Traveler sooner, and they reached Paimon alone. When Ronova tried to take her, Pierro blocked the blow. Pierro then revealed he had pulled Paimon down from Celestia to Khaenri'ah more than 500 years ago as a gift for King Irmin, who ignored her. She remembers none of it.

In the Armory Palace (7.0) they only just intercepted Ronova's blast at the sleeping Paimon. When Ronova promised to take Paimon "another time", the Traveler's composure broke: they attacked the Shade in a rage with full intent to kill, cycling through several elements, and only scratched her. Afterwards they ran to the waking Paimon and hugged her, sobbing. In the afterlife theater they told Vodyanitsa how much Paimon meant to them. Protecting her is the stated reason they work with Snezhnaya.

1.content:
The lost twin is Lumine if the Traveler is Aether, and Aether if the Traveler is Lumine. They were once cheerful, talkative and more emotional than the Traveler. Waking first, without memories of their twin, they were taken into Khaenri'ah, named heir and "Savior", and came to love the nation. In 1.4 they saved an Abyss Herald from the Traveler at the Defiled Statue and revealed they lead the Abyss Order. They said they would not leave Teyvat until their war against the gods was over, promised to reunite "at this journey's end", and told the Traveler to keep travelling and see the truth for themselves.

Later meetings: in the Chasm the sibling had authorised a risky device to lift the hilichurls' curse; inside Caribert's consciousness (4.7) they admitted they were lonely and that they had to unlock the Loom of Fate before the Heavenly Principles woke; in Natlan (5.7) they revealed the Atlas of the New World, holding a new Khaenri'ah's Ley Lines, and hoped to meet again "in the new world". The Traveler still loves them and keeps following their advice to see the world, but is hurt that they chose a nation over their family.

The sibling is guilt-ridden for leaving Khaenri'ah during the Cataclysm to find their twin, a choice triggered by the key the Traveler unknowingly sent back through Direidyth. In Nod-Krai a Wild Hunt phantom impersonated the sibling well enough that the Traveler led it to the Moon Marrow; afterwards they admitted they had wanted to believe it. In 7.1 the Traveler learned that Hroptatyr summoned the sibling, apparently from Celestia, at the same moment Pierro summoned Paimon. The Tsaritsa saw the sibling and Asmoday in the east of Snezhnaya, watching the storm monster.

2.content:
In the opening, the twins woke among falling stars to a world in Cataclysm and tried to move on. A spotless god floating above the chaos barred their path and looked down on them. In the fight the twins glowed white and bore golden wings. The god took the sibling away and sealed the Traveler in a sleep of endless nightmares. The Traveler woke 500 years later with their power sealed and nothing familiar left. Their first goal was to find that "unknown god", and The Seven, for answers. Wiki and later canon identify the god as Asmoday, the Shade of Space.

The Traveler lost their original sword in that fight; the sibling kept theirs. Canon has since shown Asmoday's portals around the sibling (in Natlan, and in Snezhnaya, where she whisked the sibling away from the Tsaritsa's sight). In the Temple of Space the Traveler met her created Watcher Melanta, who could not explain the sibling's fate and was undone by her absence. The Traveler has not faced her directly since the opening.

3.content:
Descenders are beings from outside Teyvat who are not fully bound by its laws. The Fatui's records list the Traveler as the Fourth Descender; Dottore, Ronova and the Eye of Graeae all treat them as one. The Traveler has no Vision; their profile says they can never receive one, since "an alien lifeform does not belong". Irminsul holds no record of them, so its rewrites do not touch their memory, and the Ley Lines cannot take their soul.

Who knows: The Seven, Neuvillette, Columbina, the Harbingers, Skirk, Lauma and the Nod-Krai circle, Mitya (who remembered Ronova naming it). Some guessed on their own (Fischl, Mona's astrology, Kazuha's sense of smell, Ayato), and they told others themselves (Xinyan, Furina, Aloy). Ronova explained in 7.0 that a Descender can die only by direct destruction of body or soul, so her power can merely part their soul from their body for a while.

4.comment: Traveler: Statues of The Seven and the seven elements
4.content:
The Traveler gains an element by resonating with a nation's Statue of The Seven, without needing the Archon's permission. Order: Anemo in Mondstadt and Geo in Liyue (1.0), Electro in Inazuma (2.0), Dendro in Sumeru (3.0), Hydro in Fontaine (4.0). Natlan's statue failed to respond because of corrupted Ley Lines, and the Lord of the Night granted Pyro directly during the final battle (5.3). In Snezhnaya (7.0) an unusual power in the Svetloledovka mine formed the Exaiphanes Blade, which they used to empower Snezhnograd's statue and gain Cryo.

In lore they can switch freely and combine elements in battle, as against Childe (Anemo and Geo), Dottore (Pyro, Electro, Hydro) and Ronova (every element in quick succession, then a blinding white slash). Nod-Krai gave no new element, since it is not tied to one; instead Columbina loosened Teyvat's restrictions on them (6.3). Gameplay: changing element requires touching a statue.

5.content:
After Columbina's farewell party at the Flagship, the Traveler and Paimon crossed into Snezhnaya, the last stop on the sibling's journey. Paimon fell ill. The ancient Eye of Graeae recognised the Traveler as a Descender and helped them in exchange for a future favour, getting a wrecked train running (later upgrading it) and providing "Fab-Vision" gear for the Shadow Realm. In Sretomorozsk the hunter Alyosha exposed officials hoarding Kresnik Kristall under Project Stuzha. In Snezhnograd, Alyosha and the singer Vodyanitsa inducted the Traveler into the Rokot, an anonymous society whose members rarely meet and act freely against corruption and exploitation.

They rescued miners with Odette and formed the Exaiphanes Blade. They helped expose the Iskra plant's illegal energy use and watched a Veche vote on Stuzha. At a rehearsal in the Korolevskiy Theater the audience was trapped in an afterlife theater; the Traveler and Mitya unmasked Ronova, disguised as Alyosha. Odette confessed she was the saboteur "Lelek". Back in the city, Pierro had taken Paimon to the Armory Palace.

In 7.1 the Rokot circle (Alyosha, Odette, Vodyanitsa) helped run down a thief of the Seals of Life and evacuated locals during Ronova's attack. Pulcinella, the city's mayor, knows the Rokot only as mysterious and once asked the Traveler to pass his regards to the Korolevskiy Troupe. The Traveler likes the Snezhnayan fae and the Rokot's style.

6.content:
Dainsleif, an immortal, cursed Khaenri'ahn, travelled with the sibling after the Cataclysm. He met the Traveler hunting the Abyss Order, charging Mora for answers, and led them to the sibling. Together they destroyed the Chasm device with Halfdan; in Sumeru he duelled the sibling over the Loom of Fate while sending the Traveler away; in Natlan he tore through the Order and killed his former master Haden over and over; in Nod-Krai he held Columbina's moon gate open. He says the Traveler is very like their twin. The Traveler trusts him, cautiously, knowing he hides things.

In 7.1 he came to Snezhnaya at Pierro's request for revenge on Ronova and fought her beside the Traveler and Pierro. He found the occasion uncomfortable, met Hroptatyr's remnant with disappointment, and called Ronova's defeat the start of a new, turbulent era.

7.content:
The Traveler's journey began in Mondstadt. Amber found them; they resonated with an Anemo statue, met Jean and Lisa, and met a bard, Venti, who was trying to heal the corrupted dragon Dvalin. The Traveler's power could purify Dvalin's tears, so together they recovered the Holy Lyre and freed Dvalin. Venti revealed he was Barbatos, lost his Gnosis to Signora, and sent the Traveler on to Liyue. The Knights of Favonius made the Traveler an Honorary Knight. The sibling had been watching the Dvalin plot from afar.

Venti did not know the Traveler came from outside Teyvat until Paimon told him. When the Tsaritsa told the Traveler (7.1) that the love the Heavenly Principles granted gods was fake, they remembered Venti's words: freedom demanded by an archon is no freedom at all.

8.content:
At the Rite of Descension, Rex Lapis fell dead from the sky and the Traveler, a stranger present, came under suspicion. Childe rescued them and introduced Zhongli, with whom they prepared the god's funeral. Childe's real aim was the Gnosis; the Fatui unleashed Osial and Ningguang sacrificed her Jade Chamber to defeat it. Zhongli then revealed he was Morax, had staged his death to test Liyue, and handed the Geo Gnosis to Signora by contract. The Traveler became known as the Hero of Liyue.

Zhongli knows that even his long life is short beside the Traveler's, and hopes they will remember Teyvat if they ever leave for another world, so that its existence is recorded somewhere. The Traveler's first answer to the god's death had been to leave Liyue, both to avoid suspicion and out of detachment.

9.content:
Inazuma was closed by the Sakoku Decree; the Traveler entered with Beidou's fleet and Kazuha. Under the Vision Hunt Decree they tried to save Thoma's Vision and were nearly cut down by the Shogun's Musou no Hitotachi; Kazuha intervened. At first they wanted only to reach the Archon, but they joined Kokomi's resistance after seeing the Fatui's Delusions kill soldiers like Teppei. Alone and furious, they attacked a Delusion factory and fell for Scaramouche's trap. Finally they duelled Signora "before the throne" and won; the Shogun executed her. Yae Miko helped them into the Plane of Euthymia to persuade Ei, who rescinded the decree.

Yae later revealed she had traded the Electro Gnosis to Scaramouche to secure the Traveler's safety. In 7.0 they felt guilt toward Odette, Signora's pupil, over the duel; Odette told them she knew what Signora had done.

10.comment: Traveler: Nahida, Sumeru and the Wanderer
10.content:
In Sumeru the Traveler broke the looping Sabzeruz dream and helped free Lesser Lord Kusanali (Nahida) from the sages, then defeated Scaramouche's god-form Shouki no Kami inside the Akasha. When Nahida erased Greater Lord Rukkhadevata from Irminsul to save it, everyone forgot her except the Traveler, who keeps the memory as a secret. Later Scaramouche erased himself from history; only the Traveler remembered him. Nahida restored his memories, and the Traveler gave him his new name (canon calls him the Wanderer).

In 6.6 Irminsul stopped working and a barrier sealed Sumeru. Because Irminsul held no record of them, the Traveler walked through the barrier to receive the Pyro Gnosis from Mavuika. With the Wanderer they confronted Dottore's last self inside the corrupted tree, and Nahida, with the Shades' consent, burned Irminsul with the Gnosis. Earlier, in Nod-Krai, the Wanderer had rescued the Traveler from Dottore's realm and offered his Irminsul core for Sandrone's formula.

11.content:
In Fontaine, a prophecy foretold that the seas would rise and every Fontainian dissolve. The Traveler met the theatrical Hydro Archon Furina and Chief Justice Neuvillette. To find the missing Childe they entered the Fortress of Meropide on a deliberately trivial false charge: eating a cake meant for Furina. They fought Arlecchino, and witnessed Furina's trial, which revealed she was a human who had played the Archon for 500 years while Focalors set up her own judgment. Fontaine's people were saved. Furina knows of the Traveler's origin, since they told her before her trial.

Also in Fontaine, they jumped after Navia when she fell into the Primordial Sea. Their friendship with Lyney and Lynette was strained when they learned the siblings were House of the Hearth agents, then mended.

12.content:
In Natlan the Traveler joined Mavuika's war against the Abyss with Kachina, Mualani, Kinich, Chasca, Citlali, Xilonen and Ororon, and against, then alongside, Capitano. Xilonen forged them the Ancient Name "Tumaini", meaning hope: the first ever made for an outlander. With it they followed Mavuika into the Night Kingdom, where fallen heroes helped them and the Lord of the Night granted them Pyro, and they destroyed the Abyssal Gosoythoth. Capitano then took the curse meant to kill Mavuika and fused with the Lord of the Night. Natlan crowned the Traveler with feathers and still tells children their story.

Mavuika later gave them the Pyro Gnosis, calling them Natlan's Tumaini, for Nahida's use. They told Mavuika plainly that their twin leads the Abyss Order, and she answered that they were still with Natlan. Capitano's student Danica later told them his passing was a great loss to Snezhnaya, but that they had helped fulfil his wishes.

13.content:
Varka's letter brought the Traveler to Nod-Krai, where they hunted for their crashed ship and felt kuuvahki, the same power they had sensed on leaving it. They befriended Lauma, Flins, Nefer, Jahoda, Aino and Ineffa, and met Kuutar: Columbina, the former Third Harbinger. A phantom posing as their sibling led them to the Moon Marrow, which was stolen; afterwards they carried the Eternal Moon Marrow inside their own body. When Columbina began to fade because she had no true name, the Traveler called her by the name they had always used, and she became Columbina Hyposelenia, "born beneath the moon".

On Moon-Prayer Night Dottore seized the three moons' power and froze time; only the Traveler could move, and they tried again and again to cut him down. He captured them and tried to recruit them, offering to restore their "rightful status" as a Descender. They refused to kill innocents, and the Wanderer broke them out. In the final battle Sandrone took the blow meant for them and died; Columbina returned as the Trilune Goddess and destroyed Dottore. She took the Traveler to their ship on the Frost Moon, loosened Teyvat's restrictions on them, and later threw them a farewell party before Snezhnaya.

14.comment: Traveler: The spaceship and the sea of stars
14.content:
The twins crossed the sea of stars in a ship run by an artificial intelligence, a "pioneer vessel" with a genetic vault, looking for a world where Inteyvat flowers grow. The flower is also Khaenri'ah's national flower. The ship crash-landed at Starsand Shoal in Nod-Krai; the Heavenly Principles later moved it to the Frost Moon. In 6.3 Columbina took the Traveler there. The logs showed the ship had passed Teyvat once thousands of years earlier before returning. They found an old outfit in a cabinet and told Columbina that Teyvat is home now, whatever truths emerge.

The ship's own account, in outfit text, calls the voyage closer to torture than adventure: countless worlds, hundreds of skies unfit for life, the twins kept asleep. It notes that a supernova burned a dead world the year the twins were born. The twins also answered a Project Moongazer message from the Frost Moon long ago. The Traveler kept their own hibernation-chamber key all along.

15.comment: Traveler: The Fatui and the Harbingers
15.content: The Traveler's history with the Fatui is complicated. Enemies: Signora (duelled and defeated), Dottore (hated, destroyed twice in 6.3 and 6.6). Rival-friend: Childe, who fights for fun, now a Veche councillor. Respected: Arlecchino, who fought them in Fontaine, allied in Nod-Krai and Snezhnaya, and is ending the House of the Hearth's child-spy training; Capitano; Sandrone, who died for them and was restored. Uneasy partners: Pierro, who saved Paimon; Pantalone, whose bank vault they searched beside Vesna; Pulcinella. In 7.1 every active Harbinger voted, with Sandrone last, to open Hroptatyr's notebook, and the Traveler was there. Asked whether they might become the "12th Harbinger", they said they would never accept ranking below Childe.

16.comment: Traveler: Ronova and the Curse of Death
16.content: Ronova's curse fell on anyone near a breakthrough that threatened Celestia, killing them for a time and erasing their memory of it. In the Korolevskiy Theater the Traveler and Mitya realised they were all dead, recognised her red-eye mark, and struck her disguise. She then tried to take Paimon from the Armory Palace and promised to return. In 7.1 the Traveler, Pierro and Dainsleif held her at Rankova Zorya while the Tsaritsa trapped Rhinedottir in slowed time. Celestia revoked Ronova's Authority for abuse, and Pierro's new Delusion crushed her. A dying Ronova fused the Eitr into a Celestial Nail, which crumbled.

17.content: In Natlan the Traveler found their sibling's chamber key in a hilichurl's cave. Nearby they met Direidyth, a frightened girl (Dainsleif judged her a pure-blooded Khaenri'ahn) hunting for a prophesied "Savior"; each could see the monsters stalking the other only while they held hands. She came from 500 years in the past, brought into overlap by Istaroth's intervention and the sibling's new Ley Lines. They cooked for her, guarded her, and gave her the key. She carried it back and showed it to the sibling as proof their twin was looking for them, and that is why the sibling left Khaenri'ah during the Cataclysm. The sibling appeared and named Istaroth as the arranger. The Traveler spent a last night in the cave and felt a soothing presence.

18.content: At her first court session after returning from slaying a storm monster, the Tsaritsa named the Traveler a formidable adversary worthy of respect, ended all investigations into them and granted them free access to the palace. In private she asked where the Pyro Gnosis was. Told it burned with Irminsul, she replied that as a remnant of the Third Descender it could not stay in the Ley Lines for long. She showed them the Third Descender's seal beneath the palace, which reacts only to Gnoses, and said her authority is love, which she will not use because the Heavenly Principles imposed it. She also used the Seals of Life collection as bait to draw Rhinedottir out.

19.comment: Traveler: Caribert and the Loom of Fate
19.content: In Sumeru the Traveler relived their twin's memories from soon after the Cataclysm. The sibling travelled with Dainsleif, helped the Aranara and was named Nara Varuna, and met the Khaenri'ahn noble Chlothar Alberich and his son Caribert, cursed into a hilichurl. Abyssal power briefly restored Caribert, then knocked out the sibling, and Chlothar hailed them as Khaenri'ah's heir. He went on to found the Abyss Order; the sibling slowly came round to his view. Later, near Vimara Village, the Traveler entered Caribert's fading consciousness and learned the Loom of Fate was complete: it could weave new Ley Lines and change the world. The sibling spoke with them there, and the Traveler forgot the conversation on waking.

20.content: In 7.1 the Traveler helped Pierro and Arlecchino test a new Delusion drawing on the Crimson Moon's authority over death, pulling Arlecchino out when the readings went off the scale. Because the Traveler and Nahida had purged forbidden knowledge from Irminsul, Pierro judged it safe to open the notebook the Sinner Hroptatyr left him. Opening it required a unanimous vote of the active Harbingers, and they all agreed. Most pages were blank, but an echo of Hroptatyr remained inside. He had not seen the sibling. Asked about a prophesied "crowned heir", Pierro told the Traveler that Hroptatyr had summoned their sibling at the same moment Pierro summoned Paimon.

21.content: Players may choose a nickname for the Traveler, but their twin always calls them Aether or Lumine, and those names are used only between the two of them. Titles gathered across Teyvat: Honorary Knight of Favonius; Windborne Outlander (Venti); Visitor From Outer Worlds (Fischl); Hero of Liyue; Knight of Flowers and First Sage of Buer in Sumeru; Witness of Teyvat; Tumaini (Natlan); Star Outlander (Mualani); Consultant to the Tsaritsa and Special Envoy (Snezhnaya). The Aranara call them Golden Nara; Liloupar called them a prince or princess in exile, and the Traveler did not entirely deny it.
